reason: The passage demonstrates that agency is not exclusive to leaders. While Ahab, Jezebel, and Elijah (all in leadership positions) clearly exercise agency, the text also shows non-leaders exhibiting agency: the angel independently nourishes Elijah without explicit command, and most significantly, Elisha—presented as a farmer/plowman with no prior leadership status—actively chooses to abandon his oxen and livelihood to follow Elijah and serve as his successor. Even Elijah's servant exercises limited agency in being stationed at a location. The narrative reveals a spectrum of agency across different social positions, contradicting the exclusive claim.
